The policy uses a two-layer network to implement a simple but effective Breakout strategy: when the ball is in the lower half (y > 4), the paddle chases a predicted landing position based on the ball's current x and horizontal direction (dx); when the ball is in the upper half, the paddle moves to the center (x=4.5). The first layer extracts discrete features (paddle x, ball x, ball vertical half, dx, dy) using high-weight threshold units. The second layer contains 21 "gated difference" units – 20 for each (ball_x, dx) pair in the lower half, and one for the upper half – each computing tanh(w_diff·(paddle_x – target_x)) when its condition holds, otherwise –1. The output layer sums these units with appropriate signs and biases to produce logits for LEFT and RIGHT that are approximately ±tanh(w_diff·diff), making the policy nearly deterministic. Other actions receive very negative logits.
